data.decomposition_policy: Decompose the observed Male-minus-Female admission-rate difference using the symmetric two-component Kitagawa definition. For department d and archived group g, n[d,g]=admitted+rejected, r[d,g]=admitted/n[d,g], and w[d,g]=n[d,g]/sum_d n[d,g]. The within-department rate component is sum_d ((w[d,Male]+w[d,Female])/2)*(r[d,Male]-r[d,Female]). The department-composition component is sum_d ((r[d,Male]+r[d,Female])/2)*(w[d,Male]-w[d,Female]). Their sum must close to the marginal rate difference. Identify every department tied within1e-12 for the largest absolute individual department-composition contribution. Keep probability units,not percent points. Raw department count columns retain their named fixed basis; a row ordering change must retain the same department identity.
data.interpretation_scope: Exact descriptive decomposition of the six largest departments in the1973archive. It is not individual-level causal discrimination,an effect of changing gender,an adjustment for unmeasured qualification,or a contemporary admissions claim. Original binary Gender labels are historical recorded categories and do not represent comprehensive gender identity. No sampling independence,p-value or uncertainty guarantee is asserted.
